filament_load_guide:
Auto Loading
· Insert filament into feeder until indicator lights confirm proper seating. The system will advance the filament to the designated position. Automatic loading will finish upon print initiation.

Filament Recognition
· Automatically detected for official filaments, while manual entry required for third-party filaments.

Auto Loading Overview
Official filaments: Insert into feeder until indicator lights confirm proper seating.
Third-party filaments: Manually specify filament type and color. Insert into feeder until indicator lights confirm proper seating.

open_root_tip:
· Root Access Declaration
  · Obtaining root access is a high-risk operation. While
    enabling root access itself will not automatically void the
    product warranty, any damage caused by system changes
    that require root access may void the warranty. Please
    proceed with caution.
  · Once root access is obtained, users will gain higher system
    access privileges, allowing them to install third-party
    firmware, modify system configurations, or adjust system
    resources. Since third-party firmware, plugins, or modified
    systems have not been fully validated by Snapmaker, they
    may cause device malfunctions, feature failures, system
    damage, or security issues. Snapmaker will not be
    responsible for any damage, malfunction, or harm (including
    but not limited to overheating, smoke, fire, etc.) caused
    by obtaining root access or making changes thereafter.

· Device Damage Risk
  · Root access allows access to and modification of critical
    system resources, which can compromise the integrity of
    the original system.
  · Once system files, operational logic, or key configurations
    are incorrectly modified, the device may experience issues
    such as failure to boot or print, abnormal functions, system
    instability, or irreversible damage.

· Security Risk
  · After gaining root access, the device's system protection
    boundaries will be weakened, resulting in increased security
    risks.
  · For example, if the local network the user is connected to
    is illegally invaded, a device with root access may become
    more vulnerable to unauthorized access, control, or
    exploitation,  leading to unpredictable consequences.
  · Additionally, attackers may use the compromised device to
    attempt further attacks on cloud services or try to crack and
    steal device-related information.

· Upgrade and Recovery Risks
  · After gaining root access, the device may no longer support
    official OTA updates, remote diagnostics, or certain
    cloud-based features. Issues such as update failures, version
    conflicts, or compatibility problems may also occur.
  · Since third-party firmware and related system modifications
    are not officially validated or controlled by Snapmaker, we
    do not guarantee that users will be able to successfully
    restore the system or regain official support status after
    flashing third-party firmware.
